expectation: Membrane rings on helper T cells, common in lamina propria and dense in lymphoid aggregates/follicle T zones; dimmer on scattered macrophages/monocytes. In gut: lamina propria cores of villi, not epithelium.
notes: CD4 marks membrane rings on many cells in the lymphoid aggregate, overlapping CD3E-positive cells. At tissue scale it fills the lamina propria cores of the gut wall, not the epithelium. The bright blobs in B are debris and do not affect the verdict.
observed: A: yellow follows lamina propria/mucosal cores, not epithelium or outline. B/C: epithelium mostly negative, a few bright debris blobs. D: small cluster of ringed cells. E1: dense membrane rings; E3 rings sit on CD3E+ cells.
why: Crisp membrane-ring cells, dense in the lymphoid aggregate and colocalising with CD3E, and sitting in the lamina propria, are a specific T-helper population.
